front_blocks.md: Describe the events that take place at a **synapse**. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: The events at a synapse are as follows:

- **neurotransmitters** are released from vesicles
- neurotransmitters **diffuse** across the gap between neurones
- neurotransmitters** bind** to receptor molecules on the second neurone
- a **new electrical impulse** is generated in the second neurone

front_blocks.md: What happens to the ciliary muscles, suspensory ligaments and lens when focusing on a **near object**? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: When focusing on a near object:

- The ciliary muscles **contract**
- The suspensory ligaments **loosen**
This causes the lens to become **thicker** (more curved),** increasing refraction** of light for close vision.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When focusing on a distant object the ciliary muscles relax and the suspensory ligaments loosen. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **False.**
When focusing on a distant object:

- The ciliary muscles** relax**
- The suspensory ligaments **tighten**
This pulls on the lens, making it **thinner**; this **reduces refraction** of light for distant vision.

![Diagram of skin layers showing hair follicles. Labels identify parts: A - the muscle attached to the base of a hair, B - a gland at the base of a hair, C - a hair, and D - a blood vessel.](assets/77a5ed74cb93-13955-skin-structure.png)
cards.back_md:
Structures A-D are:

- A = hair erector muscle
- B = sweat gland
- C = hair
- D = blood vessel

![Diagram of skin layers showing hair follicles. Labels identify parts: A - the muscle attached to the base of a hair, B - a gland at the base of a hair, C - a hair, and D - a blood vessel.](assets/77a5ed74cb93-13955-skin-structure.png)

front_blocks.md: How does **sweating** increase heat loss from the body? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Sweating increases heat loss when sweat** evaporates **from the skin surface. The evaporation of sweat **transfers heat energy** away from the skin.

front_blocks.md: How does **shivering** contribute towards temperature regulation? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Shivering aids temperature regulation because the rapid muscle contractions **generate heat** through** respiration**; this helps to** raise the core body temperature**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The hair erector muscles in the skin contract in response to cold temperatures. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Contraction of the hair erector muscles causes the **hairs on the skin surface to stand up**, providing a **layer of insulation** in cold temperatures.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **vasodilation**. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Vasodilation is a cooling mechanism in which the **diameter of skin arterioles increases**. This** increases blood flow **to capillaries in the skin surface, transferring heat to the environment by** radiation**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
When a person enters a colder environment blood flow to the surface of the skin is reduced. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **True.**

Vasoconstriction** **is a heat retention mechanism. The **diameter of skin arterioles decreases** to **reduce blood flow to capillaries** in the surface of the skin. This minimises heat loss by radiation.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Constriction of the capillaries reduces blood flow to the surface of the skin. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Capillaries **do not have a muscle layer **and therefore** cannot constrict**. Constriction occurs in the *arterioles that supply the skin capillaries*, reducing blood flow to the skin surface.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **gravitropism** (or geotropism).

back_blocks.md: Gravitropism, also known as geotropism, is the **directional growth** response of plants towards or away from **gravity**; roots grow downwards and shoots grow upwards.

front_blocks.md: Define the term **phototropism**.

back_blocks.md: Phototropism is the** directional growth** of plants towards or away from** light**, allowing shoots to grow towards light to optimise photosynthesis.

cards.front_md: Define the term **phototropism**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
In an investigation into the effect of gravity on newly germinated seedlings the dependent variable is the direction of gravity.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
In an investigation into the effect of gravity on newly germinated seedlings the dependent variable is the **length **and/or** direction of growth** of newly grown **roots** and **shoots**.
The direction of gravity is the independent variable in this investigation.

front_blocks.md: Which variables need to be **controlled** in an investigation into the effect of **light** on newly germinated seedlings?

back_blocks.md: Variables that need to be controlled in an investigation into the effect of light on newly germinated seedlings include:

- direction of gravity
- temperature
- water availability / how damp the cotton wool is
- type / size / age of seedlings

Phototropism is an example of chemical control of plant growth. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **True.**
Phototropism is a growth response controlled by the plant chemical **auxin**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Auxin is produced on the shady side of a plant shoot. (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Auxin is **produced in the shoot tip** before **diffusing** to the shady part of the plant.

front_blocks.md: What happens to **auxin distribution **when light shines on one side of a shoot? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: When light shines on one side of a shoot the auxin produced in the tip **accumulates on the shaded side**.

cards.front_md: What happens to **auxin distribution **when light shines on one side of a shoot? (**Extended Tier Only**)

front_blocks.md: What effect does **auxin** have on cells in the shoots of plants? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Auxin stimulates** cell elongation** in plant shoots.

cards.front_md: What effect does **auxin** have on cells in the shoots of plants? (**Extended Tier Only**)

front_blocks.md: How does auxin distribution in response to light lead to **phototropism**? (**Extended Tier Only**)

back_blocks.md: Auxin accumulation on the shaded side of a shoot causes **cells on the shady side to elongate** at a faster rate than cells on the light side; this leads to **bending of the shoot **towards the light.
